newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian state chief urges constitution rewrite.
newsitem.headline: Australian state chief urges constitution rewrite.

text.p: The premier of the Australian state of Western Australia on Wednesday urged reform of the nation's constitution to allow states to levy their own taxes, after a landmark court ruling outlawed A$5 billion in excises.

"The lack of certainty in our ability to raise funds is just totally unacceptable. The time has come for the federal government to be proactive in relation to these tax matters.," Court told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

Australia's peak court, the High Court, on Tuesday struck a major blow to the finances of the country's six states and two territories when it declared business franchise fees on alcohol, tobacco and petrol invalid under the national constitution.
The national government has been forced to draft a A$5 billion rescue package to raise the taxes on behalf of the states and return the money to them.
"The constitution must be amended so that we set in concrete the state's ability to raise the revenues that it needs to deliver the services for which it has a responsibility," Court said.

"You should have competition between the states in relation to taxing arrangements and the states should have the flexibility to provide the taxes and services in the way that best suits their particular state."
The taxes outlawed by the court ruling account for about 16 percent of state and territory income.
The states and territories already rely on Canberra for half their income, divided up at a traditionally acrimonious annual summit of state, territory and national leaders.
A successful amendment to the constitution requires the support of a majority of the states, and majority support in each of those states.
